This step allows no shell commands, so I checked the repository through file reads instead of git commands. I read .git/HEAD, .git/config, the dev and main refs, src/ap_forecast/__init__.py, ci.py, tests/test_forecast.py and the repository's CLAUDE.md. Every remaining statement cites an input, the tool view, record:brief, record:memory or a file in the repository. No connector was needed.

claims.text: The Data Science lane's tasks TSK-03 (STORY-03) and TSK-04 (STORY-04) change only the ap_forecast repository.
Repository ap_forecast (Python 3.9, standard library) is available locally, and the agent identity has write access with a clean git status.
Branch feature/story was created from dev at d67e866, and HEAD is on feature/story.
Locally, dev and main point to the same commit, d67e8662907401467a3f76f9f167e7a60d89ffca.
Remote origin is configured, and local main and dev track it. There is no upstream entry for feature/story.
No repository creation is needed: the package src/ap_forecast already exists with predict_delay_days and build_explanation_request, and tests are in tests/test_forecast.py.
The current ap_forecast version is 0.9.0, and TSK-03 owns the version step.
The CI command is /usr/bin/python3 ci.py. It enforces line coverage >= 90% and static checks that stand in for SonarQube.
The ci.py static checks flag print, eval and exec calls, bare except and lines longer than 140 characters. ci.py imports the coverage package.
Existing public signatures are kept, and new behaviour goes into new functions.
No repository uses Databricks or a database, so no Databricks or other workspace access is required.
Commit messages start with the story ID, and branches follow main, dev and feature/<story>.

open_questions: RAQ-1 (non-blocking): The working branch is literally named 'feature/story', but the convention is feature/<story> and this lane covers STORY-03 and STORY-04. Should the branch keep this name or be split or renamed per story? Interim answer: use the existing branch and keep the story ID as the commit prefix. Owner: Developer.

RAQ-2 (non-blocking): ci.py imports the third-party 'coverage' package. This step ran no shell commands, so it did not check that the package is installed for /usr/bin/python3. Interim answer: the first CI run in DS-05 or DS-06 confirms it. Owner: Developer / infra.
RAQ-3 (non-blocking): .git/config has no upstream entry for feature/story, so push rights on origin rest on the tool view's write-access statement. Owner: Developer.

I could not run git myself because this step allows no shell commands. The branch feature/story comes from dev at d67e866, and the package is at version 0.9.0. The CI command is /usr/bin/python3 ci.py, which requires at least 90% coverage. No Databricks or database is used. I removed the unsupported 'Agent actions' row. There are three open questions, none blocking: the literal branch name 'feature/story'; whether the 'coverage' package that ci.py needs is installed, which I couldn't check; and no upstream set for the branch.
